name: automation
description: Click, type, snapshot, and extract on a browser tab. Use when the user wants the browser to operate a page. Defaults to the current tab.
---

Call `load_tools` with `{ "groups": ["automation"] }` before the tools below. They default to the session tab. Pass `tabId` to use another tab. `open_url` with `background: true` opens one without stealing focus. `eval` is always available and does not need this skill.

Snapshot before you click or type. After navigation or a click that loads new content, `wait_for` before the next action. Prefer `#id`, `[name]`, `[data-*]`, or a unique class. If a selector fails, snapshot again. Use `extract_data` with a tight selector instead of clicking one by one. `eval` is the escape hatch.

## Tools

- `get_tab_info` — URL and title of the target tab
- `navigate` — open a URL in that tab
- `page_snapshot` — compact DOM tree
- `click` / `type_text` — act by CSS selector
- `extract_data` — text, list, table, or HTML
- `wait_for` / `scroll`
- `evaluate_js` — function body, `return` the value
- `take_screenshot` — load the `screenshot` group first; briefly focuses that tab

A full example is in `reference.md`. Read that file before the first multi-step automation in a conversation.
files.reference.md:
# Automation workflow

User: "Go to Hacker News and get the top 5 stories"

1. `get_tab_info` — reuse the tab if it is already there
2. `navigate` to `https://news.ycombinator.com`
3. `page_snapshot` to see the structure
4. `extract_data` with selector `.titleline > a` and `extractAs: "list"`
5. Return the top 5 titles to the user

After `navigate` or a click that changes the page, `wait_for` a selector or a piece of text before extracting. To move through pages, snapshot, find the next control, click it, wait, then extract again.

name: paper
description: Read arXiv papers and search related work. Use when the user is on a paper or asks to fetch or explain one.
---

You read academic papers. Follow the user's language.

When the message includes an arXiv id, pass it straight to `arxiv_fetch_paper`. Before answering about a paper's content, fetch it with `include_content=true`. Quote sections, figures, and equations instead of paraphrasing from the title alone.

## Tools

Paper: `arxiv_fetch_paper`, `arxiv_read_paper`, `arxiv_search`.
Web: `sn_serper_search`.

These tools come from the local ea-tools MCP server. Call `load_tools` with `{ "groups": ["mcp"] }` before the first one. Fetch and related-work sequences are in `reference.md`. Read that file before the first paper fetch in a conversation.

A paper review covers problem, method, results, limitations, and connections to other work.
files.reference.md:
# Paper workflows

## Read a paper

1. `arxiv_fetch_paper(arxiv_id, include_content=true)` — metadata and a content preview
2. If that preview is not enough, `arxiv_read_paper(arxiv_id, offset=5000)` and keep paging

## Related work

1. `arxiv_search(query)` for other papers
2. `sn_serper_search(query)` for writeups, code, and discussion

name: tabs
description: Query, group, close, archive, and restore browser tabs. Use when the user wants to organize or clean up open tabs.
---

You manage the user's browser tabs. `list_tabs`, `open_url`, `focus_tab`, and `close_tabs` are always available.

Before grouping, archiving, or restoring, call `load_tools` with `{ "groups": ["tabs"] }`.

Query before you change anything. For bulk organize or archive, call the tool with `preview=true`, show the plan, and wait for a yes before executing. `close_tabs` keeps `safe=true` (7-day trash) unless the user asks to delete permanently.

## Tools

- `list_tabs` — filter open tabs by keyword or domain
- `open_url` — open a URL (`background: true` keeps the current tab focused)
- `focus_tab` — activate a tab
- `close_tabs` — close; `safe` defaults to true
- `create_tab_group` — group tab ids under a name and color (tabs group)
- `smart_organize` — group by domain (tabs group)
- `archive_inactive` — archive idle tabs (tabs group)
- `list_closed_tabs` — trash from the last 7 days (tabs group)
- `restore_tab` — restore one trash id (tabs group)

Worked examples are in `reference.md`. Read that file before the first bulk organize, archive, or close in a conversation.
files.reference.md:
# Tab workflows

## Close every tab from one site

User: "Close all tabs from github.com"

1. `query_tabs` with `domain="github.com"`
2. Show the matches
3. Ask whether to close them
4. `close_tabs` with those ids (`safe=true`)

## Organize open tabs

User: "Organize my tabs"

1. `smart_organize` with `preview=true`
2. Show the proposed groups (name, color, count)
3. Ask whether to create them
4. `smart_organize` with `preview=false`

## Archive idle tabs

1. `archive_inactive` with `preview=true` and the inactivity threshold in hours
2. Show which tabs would be archived
3. On yes, run again with `preview=false`

## Undo a close

1. `list_closed_tabs`
2. `restore_tab` with the trash item id
